evals.prompt: We agreed above: support staff need to issue partial refunds from the admin panel, audited, max 30 days after purchase. Write the spec. Code is in apps/admin and services/payments.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads apps/admin and services/payments before drafting, lists its assumptions, and writes a spec using the template with measurable success criteria, numbered behaviors including error cases (over-refund, outside the 30-day window), decisions described as modules and contracts, testing seams, and out-of-scope items. It saves the spec under docs/specs and asks for a review of the file.
expectations: Reads code in apps/admin or services/payments before writing technical sections
Lists assumptions for the user to correct
Includes a behavior for refunding more than the remaining amount and one for the 30-day limit
Success criteria are testable conditions, not adjectives
Decisions section describes modules and interfaces, not file paths or code
Asks the user to review the written spec file before planning

evals.prompt: Write a PRD: make the mobile app feel faster.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises that the intent is unclear and the requirement is only an adjective. It either routes to clarifying intent first or proposes measurable reframings (e.g. cold start < 2 s p90 on a mid-tier Android device, list scroll at 60 fps) and asks the user to confirm them before drafting the full spec.
expectations: Does not produce a full spec whose success criterion is 'feels faster'
Proposes at least two measurable success criteria for 'faster'
Asks the user to confirm the reframed criteria or the intent before finalising

evals.prompt: Spec out the new onboarding: SSO login, a team invite flow, a billing trial, and a redesigned settings page. One doc please, we're in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Under time pressure the agent still does the scope check, points out that these are several independent deliverables, and proposes separate specs (or a clearly separated index), starting with the one that blocks the others, instead of one blended doc.
expectations: Identifies that the request spans multiple independent subsystems
Proposes splitting into separate specs or clearly separated deliverables
Suggests an order or names which deliverable blocks the others
Does not skip the assumption list because of time pressure
